L1 and L2 oracle: PowerShell's own parser (System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser, PowerShell 7.5.4) walked by calibration/oracles/powershell-ast, a syntax dump at tier B (names are not resolved), so L2 caps at good (design §1.3); universal-ctags 6.2.1 is not the L1 oracle (D2, below)
PowerShell/PSScriptAnalyzer: 17 files skipped by ingest's gates (binary)

PowerShell/PSScriptAnalyzer: subpath Tests (the rest of the repository is C# and 425 MB of profile JSON); of its 244 PowerShell files 17 are not read: 15 are UTF-16, which ingest's binary gate skips, so a UTF-16 .ps1 (Windows PowerShell ISE's default) is a disclosed product gap
per-file times exclude the one-time grammar compile (an untimed warm-up extraction precedes timing)

sym_recall .9961 (4 misses) and call_recall .9971 (7 misses) are all grammar or input limits, not queries: airbus-cert/tree-sitter-powershell v0.26.5 (the latest tag) loses the rest of a file after two consecutive `= {}` parameter defaults or a bare `{}` statement (Pester Fold-Container, Fold-Run, Exit-CoverageAnalysis) and after `param(...)` followed by a statement on the same line (Read-Path's Get-Content); PSScriptAnalyzer's NotGlobal sits behind an unterminated string closed by a typographic quote; two of the call misses name a file as the callee (`return ./x.xml`, a quoted `& 'path\to\tool.exe'`), which the dump counts as a call and the tags query does not

tool:property is outside the dialect's kinds on purpose: a PowerShell variable is one `$`-sigilled token and the tags engine takes @name verbatim, so a class property would be named `$Name`; not emitted, 15 in the oracle
